https://www.clintonnc.com/contact-us.text: Contact Us Sherry Matthews – General Manager/Advertising Director (910) 592-8137 ext. 2583 About Sherry Matthews: Sherry Matthews has been publisher and sales director of The Sampson Independent since 2016. The Clinton native and graduate of Clinton High School joined the Independent 31 years ago, quickly being promoted to editor and maintaining that position until 2016, when she was given the publisher title. A journalist since 1984, she is the recipient of four N.C. Press Association Awards, including first place honors for Editorial Writing and General News Reporting. She has also won numerous North Carolina School Bell awards for her education coverage in Sampson County. She is a member of the Clinton-Sampson Rotary Club and the Sampson Regional Medical Center Foundation and a current deacon and past deacon chairwoman at her church, Warsaw Baptist. She is a past recipient of the Clinton-Sampson Chamber of Commerce’s Outstanding Member of the Year Award and a former Rotarian of the Year. Ms. Matthews has a deep love for her community and believes in the power of journalism to grow a community and tell its many stories. Her screenplay based on a 1984 murder in Sampson County was made into the movie Tarnished Notes, which was filmed in its entirety in Sampson County. Dylan Atwood – Content Writer (910) 592-8137 ext. 2590 About Dylan Atwood: Dylan Atwood was born in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and grew up in the suburbs outside of St. Louis, Missouri, before moving to Mt. Olive, NC, when he was 10. The first time he wrote content was for his middle school newspaper, where he covered the cafeteria and library. He had a lot of fun writing those pieces, but wouldn’t really start writing for fun again until his early 30s. In the meantime, Dylan fully dived into theatre and performance art, as well as photography. He felt called to start writing again, if only just for himself and a few others. He remembered how much joy he could feel in putting words together and telling stories that entertained himself and others, and maybe even inspired others. When a freelance writing job opened up, it felt to Dylan “like getting paid to breathe,” and when he landed a full-time job as a content writer, it felt like a dream. He loves what he gets to do so much. He also loves to read, watch movies, and meditate out in nature. Anthony Goodman – Editor (910) 592-8137 ext. 2587 About Anthony Goodman: Anthony Goodman is a resident of Sampson County, who grew up here and has lived here most of his life. He attended Midway district schools for many years, served as a substitute teacher for Sampson County Schools, and coached for Hobbton. He has a deep sense of pride in his community, from the top to the bottom, from Hobbton to Harrells, Midway to Mintz. Anthony started as a Content Writer for The Sampson Independent in March 2025, and was promoted to Sports Editor in October and promoted to Editor in late May of 2026. He is a proud husband and father of five. Trevon McGlone – Content Writer (910) 592-8137 ext. 2585 About Trevon McGlone: Trevon McGlone was born in Manhattan, New York and moved to Hickory, North Carolina when he was a kid. The middle child of three siblings, he began his journey into journalism when he joined The East Carolinian at East Carolina University in his junior year of college. He would eventually become a sports reporter and then during his last semester, was Sports Editor. He has been a Content Writer with The Sampson Independent since November 2025. Trevon said he loves to write stories. “It was something I used to do when I was a child, and it kind of led to my path into the world of being a journalist,” he said. He also enjoys reading, sports and learning about historical events. Hendry Jones – Advertising Sales Representative (910) 592-8137 ext. 2024 About Hendry Jones: Having recently returned to Clinton after living in Virginia and working in the title insurance industry for more than 30 years, Hendry Jones is enjoying re-learning her hometown and seeing (and recognizing!) people she has known since childhood. Working with the newspaper is giving Hendry a great opportunity to meet and work with many folks who moved to the Sampson County area, or were born, since she moved away in 1986. Brenda McCullen – Classified Director (910) 592-8137 ext. 2589 About Brenda McCullen: Brenda Rogerson McCullen is a graduate of Midway High School and Hardbarger Business College. She was married to the late Ronnie McCullen and has three precious children. She has worked at The Sampson Independent for more than 30 years, in the Classified Department, including line and display ads, as well as legals. Kim Bell – Circulation Director 910-592-8137 ext. 2581 About Kim Bell: Kim Bell of Mount Olive has been the Circulation Director for The Sampson Independent since August 2018. She has two daughters, Courtney and Shannon, and has been with the love of her life, Tony, for 18 years. She loves animals, family and dancing. Mary Royal – Assistant Circulation Manager About Mary Royal: Mary Royal has been working with The Sampson Independent since December 2017. She started as a carrier. Over the years, positions have been created for her, and she is now the Assistant Circulation Manager. A retiree from Walmart, she said, “This job gives me something to do after retirement. I love what I do and I love and enjoy the people I work with. Looking forward to many more years with them.” Manage options Manage services Manage {vendor_count} vendors Read more about these purposes {title} {title} {title}

Photograph: J Scott Applewhite/AP View image in fullscreen Ilhan Omar speaks with members of the Congressional Progressive caucus, Maxwell Frost, Pramila Jayapal and Chuy Garcia, in Washington DC on 13 January. Photograph: J Scott Applewhite/AP Ilhan Omar Democrats rebuke federal raid of Ilhan Omar’s home: ‘rogue abuse of power’ Top House Democrats question the ‘corrupt weaponization’ of federal government against Trump’s adversaries Maya Yang Mon 12 Oct 2026 13.57 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ilhan Omar ’s Democratic colleagues have condemned federal agents’ search of the Minnesota congresswoman’s home on Monday morning, describing it as “deeply disturbing” and emblematic of the Trump administration ’s “corrupt weaponization” of the US government. House Democratic leaders, including minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, party whip Katherine Clark and caucus chair Pete Aguilar, issued a joint statement excoriating the president for the search. “The Trump administration’s raid on congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s home is deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the continued corrupt weaponization of the federal government against [the president’s] adversaries,” their statement said. Ilhan Omar says she will not be silenced after federal agents raid her home Read more “For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations. Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected member of Congress and her family.” The Democratic leaders vowed to “deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power” from the US Departments of Justice and Homeland Security, the latter of which oversees immigration enforcement. Citing unnamed sources “close to the investigation”, Fox News – which is typically friendly with the Trump administration – reported that the search on Omar’s home pertained to a criminal fraud investigation concerning her immigration paperwork. Omar’s late father filled out that paperwork when Omar, a Somali-born, naturalized US citizen, was a child. California representative Ro Khanna also condemned Monday’s search, saying : “It is simply chilling that they are targeting political opponents this way, and it is disturbing that they are targeting Muslim Americans and a Muslim American legislator. Any decent American needs to stand up and speak out.” Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Khanna’s fellow Democrat and California representative, called the search “fascism in the extreme”. “This is an unadulterated abuse of power,” Kamlager-Dove said. “Trump is weaponizing the federal government to escalate his racist attacks against [representative] Omar, undermine her ahead of the midterms [on 3 November], and distract from his failures as president.” Pramila Jayapal, a Democratic House member from Washington state, similarly called the search of Omar’s home a “disgusting abuse of power from an out of control president” facing widespread public disapproval from high living costs amid the war in Iran that he helped start alongside Israel in February. “To use federal law enforcement resources to raid the home of a sitting Member of Congress weeks before an election is a dangerous sign of an authoritarian president who will stop at nothing to distract you from his deep unpopularity with the American people,” Jayapal added. Jayapal’s statement alluded to years of unsubstantiated rumors from Trump and others about Omar and her family, including the accusation that her ex-husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, is in fact her brother – and that the marriage was part of an effort to earn him immigration status. Omar has denied those rumors. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly, plus breaking news alerts Sign up to The Stakes 2026 A weekly guide to what really matters in the US midterms, plus breaking news alerts. after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen Homeland security officers carry boxes from the Washington DC residence of Ilhan Omar on Monday during a search. Photograph: J Scott Applewhite/AP The Illinois representative Delia C Ramirez called for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to be dismantled. Omar “has not backed down, so now they are using DHS and the federal government to target and persecute her”, Ramirez said in a post on X. “This is an absolute abuse of power and unacceptable. We must strip them of their weapons. We must dismantle DHS.” Similarly, Greg Casar, a Democratic representative from Texas, wrote that the Trump administration is targeting Omar “because he thinks it’ll help his [Republican] party” during the midterms , when it is expected to lose seats in Congress. “Ilhan Omar stands up and won’t let Trump do whatever he wants to our country,” Casar said. “It’s up to us to do the same.” The Council on American-Islamic Relations (Cair), the US’s largest Muslim civil rights organization, also spoke out against the search of Omar’s home, saying : “We strongly condemn this unconscionable raid on her home for what it is: an obvious act of political persecution.” Criticizing the Trump administration’s handling of files pertaining to Jeffrey Epstein’s child sex-trafficking network as well as the president’s pardons for those who attacked the US Capitol in early 2021, Cair said the justice department “could clearly [not] care less about fighting crime and is instead focused on conducting a witch hunt”. https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-and-c.text: The EU and Canada are betting they can deepen their partnership while Donald Trump looks inward at the U.S. midterms — and before European elections upend the political calculus. Their strategy is to push for the broadest possible upgrade and hope Trump is too busy campaigning to respond, four EU officials and two Canadian diplomats familiar with preparations for this week’s summit in Montreal said. Trump, whose Republican Party is fighting to retain control of Congress in next week’s midterms, has called the EU’s offer of associate membership for Canada “laughable” and threatened “serious tariffs” if the two sides get too close. Advertisement Advertisement European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa will join Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney for two days of talks on trade, security, energy, education and the Arctic on Thursday. The summit “is a very strong statement,” said Mark Camilleri, president of the Canada and EU Trade and Investment Association. “I don’t think there’s any feeling that this is going to be some discreet get-together.” Canada is also looking to move before Europe’s politics shift. Ottawa wants changes to the partnership that will outlast Trump and Marine Le Pen, whose National Rally is polling ahead in France and has criticized the EU-Canada trade pact, CETA, said a Canadian diplomat. All the officials and diplomats in this article were granted anonymity to speak frankly about the summit preparations. Avoiding Trump’s ire Brussels and Ottawa are pushing to strengthen their relationship, including by cooperating more closely on trade and defense, international engagement and institutional links, according to a draft joint statement obtained by POLITICO . In her September State of the Union speech, von der Leyen emphasized that the EU-Canada alliance is “not against anyone else.” Yet officials acknowledge that a stronger alliance risks triggering retaliation from Trump. Von der Leyen, Costa and Carney “are fully aware that the eyes of the world are upon them,” said Camilleri. Advertisement Advertisement The Europeans and Canadians know “the U.S. is watching,” a senior EU official said, adding that the bloc and Canada were nevertheless proceeding with business as usual and pushing for the most expansive possible relationship with Ottawa. Another possibility is that the summit yields only “nice pictures” and little substance, a third senior official said, making it less likely to “trigger” the president. European capitals, EU institutions and Canada’s provinces are all waiting to see what von der Leyen and Carney agree on in their meeting, the Canadian diplomat said, adding it was impossible to pre-judge how Trump would react. Shadow of Le Pen For Ottawa, pressure comes from another direction: Europe’s electoral calendar and the rise of the far right. With Spain, France, Poland and Italy all set to go to the polls in the next year, Canadian officials want to secure concrete gains while EU governments remain receptive to closer cooperation and keep the topic front of mind, before elections across the bloc risk shifting priorities and upsetting the political balance. When Carney came to Strasbourg to lay out his vision for a closer alliance in September, he was heckled from the gallery by the far-right Alternative for Germany MEP Siegbert Droese, who led chants of “USA!” Advertisement Advertisement But it’s France’s presidential election in April — and the prospect of Le Pen in office — that is causing the most concern, according to a second Canadian diplomat. “It’s very fortunate we’re doing this summit now and not in six months,” the diplomat said, referring to the French election date. Canada is pushing for big, bold “structural changes” in its relationship with the EU now that will outlast Trump and Le Pen, the diplomat added. Carney has grasped the moment’s rarity and urgency and will not leave the summit without securing major wins, the first Canadian diplomat said. Another question is whether Brussels and Ottawa can upgrade their partnership without eventually drawing the U.S. president’s ire. The midterms might buy them some time, but the vote will not keep Trump busy forever. Trump might be even more dangerous and more likely to take out his anger on the EU and Canada after the election, given that he will retain many of his tariff and foreign policy powers even if the Republicans lose Congress, the second Canadian diplomat warned. “At the end of the day, his reaction could be anything,” Camilleri said. “We can only control what we can control.” Mathieu Pollet contributed reporting.
